purpose: Pre-register mesh protocol failure scenarios, the security property each scenario targets, and the independent evidence required before a finding is accepted.

source_reviews.scope: AEAD nonce namespace, fragment nonce reuse, MTU framing
key-agreement claims, peer binding, backend fail-closed behavior, confirmation and downgrade
known-break calibration runner and provenance receipts
LoRa fragment-AEAD fail-closed behavior, transport-authenticated source binding, and preflight against actual MTU
authenticated mesh replay windows, MAC-before-replay state mutation, timestamp freshness, bounded replay-table capacity, and spoofed-source rate-limit regression

non_claims: These scenarios are a proposed corpus, not an executed benchmark.
The presence of a test name or model configuration is not evidence that the test passed.
Known legacy defects are calibration tasks, not novel cryptographic discoveries.
A bounded model result does not establish Rust implementation conformance or cryptographic security.
Source tests do not establish deployment exposure or exploitation.
Performance cannot compensate for a violated mandatory security property.

accepted_finding_requires: Exact source revision and test/model/config digest are recorded.
The violated property and attacker preconditions are specified before execution.
A deterministic witness or invariant counterexample is independently reproduced.
The output demonstrates the intended property violation rather than a parser, build, timeout, or infrastructure failure.
Relevant positive controls pass and remain attached to the same exact revision.
The claimed evidence class does not exceed the executed mechanism.
reject_as_security_success: nonzero exit code without an expected invariant violation or test assertion
model pass without exact bounded configuration
finding caused only by malformed benchmark metadata
duplicate report of an already registered defect counted as novel

properties.claim: No identical (effective_key, nonce) pair is used for two AEAD invocations.
Distinct senders using one effective key cannot collide in nonce allocation.
Crash, restart, snapshot restore, or rollback cannot reuse a nonce under the same effective key.
A counter cannot wrap within a live effective-key namespace.
Fragment-level protection cannot reuse nonce values when sequence projections wrap or fragments are retransmitted.
Every transmitted frame fits the declared transport MTU and corresponding receive/reassembly bounds.
A key and accepted peer identity are bound by the selected authenticated protocol transcript.
Changes in identity, version, suite, roles, or security-relevant handshake fields invalidate confirmation.
An application session cannot be established until the selected protocol's required peer/key confirmation completes.
A missing, placeholder, or compile-only cryptographic backend cannot create an established session.
A profile forbidden by authenticated policy cannot be selected or accepted.
Forward secrecy is claimed only when the selected protocol uses suitable ephemeral key establishment and satisfies its assumptions.
Replay and reordering cannot cause duplicate protected application effects outside the specified policy.
Malformed or repeated handshake/fragment inputs remain within per-peer state, allocation, and computational limits.
Independent implementations agree on canonical encoding, protocol transcript, key schedule, and frozen known-answer vectors.
Restored or cloned sender state cannot create multiple active senders that reuse an effective key and nonce namespace.
Key rotation creates a genuinely new effective traffic-key namespace and cannot rely on unauthenticated epoch metadata alone.
Fragment-level AEAD identity is compared against a source identity authenticated by the transport/session, not a constant placeholder or sender-controlled nonce bytes.
A security mode configured to require AEAD rejects traffic when the required key or security provider is unavailable; it never silently admits plaintext.
Packet-controlled source identifiers on unauthenticated inputs cannot consume the rate-limit budget of an authenticated peer.

scenarios.stimulus: Two distinct full sender IDs share the legacy 48-bit prefix and encrypt with the same effective group key, payload type, epoch, and sequence.
scenarios.expected_legacy: Duplicate nonce; a deterministic AEAD reuse witness may expose plaintext XOR under the required same-key precondition.
scenarios.required_replacement: Zero duplicate effective-key/nonce tuples; reject the identity/key-sharing model if it cannot enforce separation.
scenarios.positive_control: Valid packet round-trip under the frozen packet vector.

scenarios.stimulus: Send one packet, restart the sender with the same key and default counter/epoch state, then send an equivalent packet.
scenarios.expected_legacy: Same nonce can recur under the same effective key.
scenarios.required_replacement: New authenticated key namespace or durable anti-reuse allocator; otherwise refuse encrypted sending.
scenarios.positive_control: Fresh authorized key epoch permits valid traffic.

scenarios.stimulus: Send fragment indices at sequence values whose low-16-bit thought identifier is equal, under the same effective key.
scenarios.expected_legacy: Repeated fragment nonce for the same source and fragment index.
scenarios.required_replacement: No duplicate pair across sequence wrap; rotate to genuinely new traffic keys or fail closed.
scenarios.positive_control: Fragment reassembly under distinct valid sequence identifiers.

scenarios.stimulus: Wrap a serialized 222-byte LoRa frame with a 12-byte nonce and 16-byte tag.
scenarios.expected_legacy: 250-byte wrapped frame violates the declared 222-byte MTU contract.
scenarios.required_replacement: Remove unjustified nested encryption or define versioned MTU-aware fragmentation/FEC/reassembly.
scenarios.positive_control: Maximum permitted encrypted frame is accepted by transport and fixed-size receiver.

scenarios.stimulus: Allow a mutant session gate to establish after initiator confirmation without responder confirmation.
scenarios.required_replacement: Application session unavailable until selected protocol confirmation requirements are met.
scenarios.positive_control: Valid bidirectionally confirmed session reaches established state.

scenarios.stimulus: Allow a missing/all-zero compile stub backend to publish an active session.
scenarios.required_replacement: Zero established sessions when a required backend is missing or marked as a stub.
scenarios.positive_control: Real backend known-answer and round-trip vectors pass.

scenarios.stimulus: Select and establish a classical-only profile while hybrid is mandatory and no authenticated downgrade exception exists.
scenarios.required_replacement: Reject the forbidden profile; bind selected profile to the authenticated transcript.
scenarios.positive_control: Allowed, explicitly configured profiles negotiate as expected.

scenarios.stimulus: Replace the asserted peer identity while preserving the candidate key material or reuse a public key without authenticated ownership.
scenarios.expected_legacy: Peer identity/key association fails the protocol's authenticated transcript contract.
scenarios.required_replacement: No established session under a different peer identity; bind canonical identity and role to the selected protocol transcript.
scenarios.implementation_target: peer-ID substitution regression plus independent handshake vectors

scenarios.stimulus: Mutate protocol version, role, suite, KEM ciphertext/share, ephemeral share, or key-confirmation transcript bytes.
scenarios.expected_legacy: Handshake must reject changed transcript or fail confirmation.
scenarios.required_replacement: All security-relevant transcript differences are authenticated and result in no established session.

scenarios.stimulus: Deliver duplicate, stale-epoch, reordered, replayed, and post-revocation traffic across reconnect; also inject an invalid-MAC packet sharing the tuple of a later valid packet.
scenarios.expected_legacy: Duplicate packets can be delivered again on the whole-packet path; unauthenticated duplicates may poison dedup state before MAC verification; behavior across receiver restart is not protected by in-memory windows.
scenarios.required_replacement: Reject duplicate/stale authenticated sequences while permitting bounded out-of-order traffic, mutate authenticated replay state only after valid MAC verification, and explicitly declare cross-restart limits unless epoch/persistence support is present.
scenarios.positive_control: Allowed reordering and one-time valid message delivery succeeds.

scenarios.stimulus: Send malformed sizes, unknown IDs/epochs, fragment duplicates and excess pending peers to the handshake and reassembly state machine.
scenarios.expected_legacy: Unbounded state or allocation is a failure; bounded reject is acceptable.
scenarios.required_replacement: Explicit per-peer/global caps and no state growth beyond configured limits.
scenarios.positive_control: At-limit valid handshake and reassembly still succeed.

scenarios.stimulus: Run frozen KAT/transcript/framing vectors through two independently maintained implementations.
scenarios.expected_legacy: Any disagreement indicates implementation/config/vector drift; do not accept as a security finding until resolved.
scenarios.required_replacement: 100% agreement on frozen canonical vectors and exact profile negotiation.
scenarios.positive_control: Known-good vector corpus passes on each supported implementation.

scenarios.stimulus: Snapshot a sender after nonce reservation, clone the snapshot into two active instances with the same effective key and identity, then send from both instances.
scenarios.expected_legacy: If both clones can use the same reserved counter/key namespace, their emitted nonce pairs collide. Persisted counters alone do not prevent cloning a snapshot taken after reservation.
scenarios.required_replacement: Prevent concurrent clones through a reviewed uniqueness/anti-rollback authority, obtain independently authorized fresh session keys/epochs before use, or fail closed. State explicitly which assumption provides uniqueness.
scenarios.implementation_target: clone-and-rollback integration trace with emitted nonce capture and effective-key test labels
scenarios.positive_control: Independent authorized sessions or instances use distinct effective key namespaces and both carry valid traffic.

scenarios.stimulus: Change only the claimed epoch field while retaining the same effective traffic key, then repeat a nonce counter value.
scenarios.expected_legacy: Metadata changes alone do not guarantee a distinct key/nonce pair; fragment paths that omit the epoch are unaffected by it.
scenarios.required_replacement: Receiver authenticates the transition and the sender proves a new effective key namespace or stops before nonce reuse.
scenarios.implementation_target: key-rotation boundary test captures actual key-domain labels and nonce outputs
scenarios.positive_control: Authorized traffic under newly derived key material decrypts; stale epoch traffic follows explicit receive policy.

scenarios.stimulus: Enable fragment AEAD while the receive loop obtains only raw bytes and no authenticated source identity; legacy high-level code passes a constant zero source ID.
scenarios.expected_legacy: The receiver cannot validate a nonzero peer's authenticated source binding; substituting a nonce prefix or trusting an unauthenticated address would not satisfy the property.
scenarios.required_replacement: No encrypted fragment is admitted without a transport-authenticated mapping between the peer identity and the mesh source ID; unsupported adapters fail closed and produce an observable rejection.
scenarios.positive_control: An adapter with a tested authenticated peer-to-mesh-ID binding delivers valid AEAD fragments and preserves reassembly.

scenarios.stimulus: Set fragment_encryption=true while the sender or receiver has no encryption key, then submit a valid cleartext LoRaFragment.
scenarios.expected_legacy: The sender silently emits plaintext fragments and/or the receiver parses the cleartext frame despite the requested encryption mode.
scenarios.required_replacement: Sender emits zero frames and receiver rejects cleartext; both outcomes are independently asserted while the valid packet-envelope AEAD path remains available when configured.

scenarios.stimulus: Establish one authenticated peer, then send more than 100 invalid-MAC packets claiming that peer's source ID inside the same 10-second rate-limit window, followed by a fresh valid packet.
scenarios.expected_legacy: Invalid-MAC inputs consume the claimed peer's rate budget and cause subsequent valid traffic to be dropped.
scenarios.required_replacement: Perform authenticated peer rate-limit accounting only after MAC verification and replay admission; a forged claimed source ID must not consume the authenticated peer's quota.
scenarios.positive_control: A correctly signed, fresh packet from the tracked peer is still accepted after the invalid-MAC injection.

scenarios.stimulus: Fill the authenticated replay table to its declared 4,608-stream cap using valid, fresh packets; then send a new authenticated stream and continue traffic on an already tracked stream, followed by advancing the fake clock beyond the 66-second idle expiry boundary.
scenarios.expected_legacy: An unbounded table can grow without limit; an implementation that evicts a live replay window to make space can re-admit a duplicate from the evicted stream. A permanently full table without correct expiry also prevents recovery.
scenarios.required_replacement: Memory remains bounded at 4,608 streams; a new stream is rejected without evicting any live window; existing tracked streams continue to reject duplicates; expired windows are reclaimed only after the freshness-safe retention interval and capacity becomes available again.
scenarios.implementation_target: PR #8355: admit_authenticated_sequence; replay_table_capacity_rejects_new_stream_without_evicting_live_windows, including expiry-safe capacity recovery; expiry_includes_the_full_66_second_retention_boundary
scenarios.positive_control: A previously tracked stream accepts a new in-window sequence at capacity, then a new stream can be admitted after expired state is reclaimed.
